id_routing.description: Interconnect may append bits to AxID to identify the originating master; slave-side ID_WIDTH > master-side ID_WIDTH
id_routing.compliance_note: Returning ID is the WIDER value; routing strips appended bits before returning to the master

fields.topology_type: Point-to-point single-drop link: one IO-Link Device connects to one port of an IO-Link Master over a single three-wire cable (L+, L-, C/Q). There is no bus, no multi-drop, and no on-wire Device addressing; the Master provides multiple independent ports, each driving exactly one Device. IO-Link is not a fieldbus.

supported_topologies.name: Point-to-point
supported_topologies.description: One Device -> one Master port over one three-wire cable (max 20 m).

supported_topologies.name: Multi-port Master
supported_topologies.description: A Master with several independent IO-Link ports, each a separate point-to-point link.

supported_topologies.name: SIO / SDCI
supported_topologies.description: The same C/Q line operates as a binary switching signal (SIO) or a communication link (SDCI).

master_slave_role_summary.description: The communication master; provides ports, issues the wake-up request, drives M-sequences, runs the Device state machine, and presents Process Data / On-request Data / Events upward. The only initiator.
The communication slave (sensor or actuator); answers Master messages, provides Process Data, serves ISDU requests, raises Events, and is described by an IODD.

fields.interconnect_role: IO-Link is a single-drop point-to-point sensor/actuator link on the C/Q line. Communication is half-duplex and Master-initiated; cyclic Process Data and acyclic On-request Data (ISDU) and Events flow over the same wire in SDCI mode, while SIO mode reuses the wire as a plain switching signal.

ordering_guarantees.m_sequence: M-sequences are exchanged in order; each is a Master message answered by a Device response.
ordering_guarantees.process_data: Cyclic Process Data is updated every cycle in OPERATE.
ordering_guarantees.isdu: Segmented ISDU transfers are reassembled in order.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: IO-Link is not memory-mapped on the wire; the Direct Parameter page (read directly) and the ISDU parameter space (Index/Subindex) are the addressable surfaces. There is no on-wire Device address — one Device per Master port.

slave_classification.polling_target: Software polls LSR.DR / THRE for non-interrupt-driven operation.
slave_classification.interrupt_target: INTR signal drives external interrupt controller; software services via IIR-identified source.
slave_classification.dma_target: TXRDY/RXRDY drive an external DMA controller for high-throughput data movement.
